reviews.decision: The exact public scrolling root exports this InjectionToken at both advertised minimum CDK versions; its complete declaration has no private, deprecated or experimental marker. The helper compares the token object by identity and returns null only during the real parent construction. A different token with the same description reaches the borrowed parent with unchanged fallback/options. The new complete-helper tests use the genuine public scrolling token with both minimum Core namespaces; the retained actual CdkTable node-constructor tests also show that later node lookups, consumer fields and projected/embedded content retain the ancestor viewport. No consumer provider is installed or changed. This closes only this source-bound public import role. Parent/service protocols and borrowed TypeScript6/Node22/RxJS7 diagnostics do not qualify a complete legacy view, real viewport/browser, compiler21, packed artifact, supported toolchain/RxJS floor, upstream SHA or whole G11. Required current rendering and full floor tests remain pending. No product HTML, CSS, SCSS or consumer files changed.

The helper uses the stable public CdkTable class as the constructor Proxy target. Both authenticated minimum public table declarations export it and the complete runtime constructor accepts zero arguments. The 21.x declaration's ignored rest-argument compatibility placeholder is recorded but unused: owned MatLegacyTable calls super() and explicitly rejects manual arguments before parent construction. The helper preserves Reflect.construct's original new.target, direct instance prototype and derived fields; no render or data-source method is replaced. The retained genuine minimum node-DI tests execute the real CdkTable constructor and focused Angular22 full/partial AOT factories. The separate OnPush review still requires current packed rendering. This closes only this source-bound public import role. This type-only stable public Core interface describes optional, self, skipSelf and host as optional booleans at both advertised minima. The owned Injector.get annotation accepts this object and forwards its original identity without cloning, converting to numeric flags or deciding lookup semantics. Strict minimum Core declaration checks select a nondeprecated get overload and reject string-valued options; the complete helper forwards all sixteen flag combinations plus undefined for three distinct non-viewport tokens. The flag matrix tests argument preservation through a protocol, while the retained genuine CdkTable node-DI comparison separately checks the actual parent's token/options sequence. The annotation erases from executable code. This closes only this source-bound public import role. The stable public abstract Injector is subclassed only to borrow the already active node injector and intercept the exact viewport token during parent construction. For all other tokens, get returns the original parent.get result and preserves token, fallback and options. It creates no owning child/application, registers no providers and invokes no destruction hook. The complete helper tests prove lookup/value identity and that only the external injector owner destroys its registered value. The retained actual minimum constructor evidence additionally forwards the original node services, including ChangeDetectorRef and later Injector lookups; the helper never substitutes an environment injector for that node. This closes only this source-bound public import role. The helper calls the stable public inject(Injector) signature synchronously while the owned table's super target is being constructed in Angular's original node context. It requests the existing Injector token before entering the temporary borrowed context, with no options or compatibility flags. Strict minimum Core checks resolve the stable generic public overload, and the retained actual minimum CdkTable node-DI receipts verify the original node/services and the same parent token/options sequence after the narrowly specified viewport normalization. The complete-helper tests independently prove that the borrowed injector remains available after super, consumer fields run in the original context, and out-of-context injection still fails normally.
